frequency_question: How often do highly contested electoral reform bills pass the U.S. Senate within a comparable legislative window when similar advance signaling is present?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone federal voting qualification or election administration bills subject to filibuster or intense partisan division, excluding routine or bipartisan unanimous consent measures.
coverage_note: 5 major legislative focal points named; represents the primary class of highly contested federal voter eligibility/administration pushes in recent decades.
known_gaps: Excludes minor rider amendments attached stealthily to omnibus appropriations bills.
skeleton: Major partisan electoral reform attempts in the Senate since 1990, categorized by whether they achieved bipartisan consensus or faced strict party-line division.
multiplier: 2 successful bipartisan/compromise major bills out of 5 prominent focal attempts over 30 years under polarized conditions yields a base rate of approximately 40% for passing major electoral legislation when pushed.
validity_reason: The baseline polarization and filibuster dynamics of the U.S. Senate remain stable through the end of the decade.
